chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammam from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid said:

I heard Muhammad ibn Ibrahim saying: Whoever leaves the Two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina) after the sun has risen, before he has prayed Dhuhr and Asr, a call will be made from behind him: May God not accompany you.

key_terms.الظُّهْرَ وَالْعَصْرَ: Dhuhr and Asr (the noon and afternoon prayers)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who leaves Mecca before praying Dhuhr and Asr?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith highlights the ritual importance of performing Dhuhr and Asr prayers within the precincts of the Two Sanctuaries before departure, reflecting the Shia emphasis on adhering to specific conditions of the Ihram state. The 'call from behind' serves as a spiritual admonition, underscoring that neglecting these obligatory prayers during the Hajj journey constitutes a deficiency in the pilgrim's ritual completeness.
